technical_and_design_decisions: Use Maven as the build tool for new separate Kafka and Rabbit test fixture repositories, aligned with existing SCDF ecosystem build standards for consistency.
Structure new test fixture repositories as Maven multi-module projects to separate core utilities from platform-specific code, maximizing reusability across consuming projects.

Implement cross-platform consistent REST APIs (U3) using a common Spring Boot controller layer with auto-configuration to abstract Lattice/YARN/CF platform-specific details, reusing existing platform adapters without modification.
Extend the existing SCDF stream DSL parser and channel registry to support named channels (U5), maintaining full backward compatibility with existing stream definition syntax.
Extend the existing SCDF artifact registry to add a 'library' artifact type (U4), with validation enforced at the DSL and API layers to restrict usage to include/exclude statements.
Leverage the existing SCDF runtime metadata store's unique constraint capabilities to enforce stream name uniqueness (U7), avoiding changes to the persistence layer.

Implement the Kinesis source module (U8) following the existing Spring Cloud Stream source module pattern used for Kafka/Rabbit sources, using AWS Kinesis SDK v2 for consistency with other AWS SCDF modules.
Use JUnit 5, Mockito, and Testcontainers for all new test coverage (U6), aligned with existing SCDF testing conventions and CI pipeline requirements.
assumptions: The existing SCDF codebase uses Java 17, Spring Boot 3.x, and Spring Cloud 2023.x, consistent with the Spring Framework 6.0 Java 17+ requirement specified in the documentation.

New separate Kafka and Rabbit test fixture repositories will be published to the existing internal SCDF Maven repository, using the same group ID as other SCDF test utilities for consistent dependency management.

Existing platform adapters for Lattice, YARN, and CF are already implemented in the SCDF codebase, so REST API consistency work (U3) only requires abstracting existing functionality, not building new platform support.
The existing SCDF stream DSL parser can be extended to support named channel syntax without introducing breaking changes to existing valid stream definitions.
The Kinesis source module (U8) will use the official AWS Kinesis SDK v2, consistent with other AWS-integrated modules in the SCDF ecosystem.

The existing SCDF runtime metadata store (e.g., H2, Redis) already supports unique constraint enforcement for stream names, so no new persistence layer changes are required for duplicate stream name prevention (U7).
Full access to existing SCDF code repositories, CI/CD pipelines, test environments, and internal Maven repository is available to the developer for all required work.
All user story requirements are fully specified, with no additional unstated requirements or edge cases beyond those implied by the provided user stories.
